claim: Sugarcane mapping benefits from multi-temporal optical and SAR information because phenological trajectories and harvest/regrowth dynamics can separate sugarcane from spectrally similar vegetation better than a single-date vegetation index.
conditions: Temporal windows must be complete, documented and aligned with the local crop calendar; optical observations require cloud and shadow quality control.
limitations: Phenology varies with region, cultivar, irrigation, planting date, ratoon status and year, so a model trained in one project is not automatically transferable.
recommended_action: Use rolling complete-period Sentinel-1 VV/VH and Sentinel-2 spectral-index features, store exact dates, and confirm local phenology before model fitting.
not_allowed_action: Do not infer a general sugarcane signature from one NDVI composite or silently include future/incomplete temporal periods.
